sourceMissing.text: The right defender moves up behind the pass. Starting roles help us share jobs as the ball moves.
The midfielder carries into the available angle. The left defender moves up behind to stay connected after the restart.
The defender takes the return away from pressure. The midfielder moves to offer another angle instead of staying beside the opponent.
After passing wide, the middle midfielder moves across behind the ball to offer a return angle.
After the forward pass, the right defender moves up behind the midfielder to remain a reachable return option.
The goalkeeper shifts toward the ball side while the defender keeps protecting the direct route.
The wide attacker carries along the side. Our right defender follows the runner while the left defender protects the middle.
Blue’s middle player moves behind the wide carrier for support. Our covering midfielder shifts with that new passing angle.
The forward receives at a useful distance again. Come closer when the pass is too long; stay ahead when the midfielder can reach you.
Coming nearer shortens this passing distance without joining the defender. With one forward, your midfield pair needs that reachable connection.
Coming nearer shortens this passing distance without joining the defender. With one forward, your midfield pair needs that reachable connection.
The outside route helped until the defender closed it. Keep a return angle behind the ball so you can choose again.
The opponent has stepped into the forward route. The middle defender remains behind and inside the pressure, offering a clear return.
The opponent has stepped into the forward route. The middle defender remains behind and inside the pressure, offering a clear return.
The pass finds you outside after the dribble. First leave your teammate room, then reconnect as their position changes.
Moving behind keeps you available without crossing the teammate’s next inside touch.
Moving behind keeps you available without crossing the teammate’s next inside touch.
The loose rebound was reachable; the controlled ball was not. Look again after a shot before deciding to chase or recover.
The keeper has secured this ball before you can reach it. Which move helps defend the next pass?
The runner moved into a permitted position before the pass. Check the rules your competition uses for its offside boundary.
The forward returns behind the second-last opponent before the teammate passes. The timing of the pass matters, not just where the run ends.
The forward returns behind the second-last opponent before the teammate passes. The timing of the pass matters, not just where the run ends.
The same restart offered different choices as Blue moved. Look at the lane before choosing the permitted pass or dribble.
Blue has stepped into the dribble route. The midfielder’s new angle opens a different route for the restart.
Blue has stepped into the dribble route. The midfielder’s new angle opens a different route for the restart.
Our nearer midfielder holds the pressure while the other moves into cover. Their carrier now faces two different defensive jobs.
Their carrier tests the pressure with a short carry. Our nearest midfielder moves with the ball, and the covering midfielder keeps a second defensive line.
Reset the two midfielders. Their distances from the carrier will decide who pressures and who covers.
Now our central midfielder is nearer and takes the pressure. Our other midfielder covers behind instead of chasing the same ball.
Their carrier moves again. Our nearer midfielder follows without crossing into the covering teammate’s path. Pressure and cover stay connected.
Return the group to the middle, then compare the danger on the other side.
Reset the midfielders so we can compare a carrier who has already escaped the pressure.
Return the ball and compare who is now protecting the space behind the attack.
Return the ball to the goalkeeper. This is a new goal-kick picture with pressure on the other side.
After the return, the left ala widens and the pivot checks short. The fixo has new receiving angles.
The fixo can keep possession, but the question asks for a forward route. The pivot is ahead and the defender has not closed that lane.
The pivot is still ahead, but the defender now stands in the passing lane. Use the deeper angle rather than the same destination.
Advancing the second rear player removes the return pass and leaves both players ahead of the ball. Keep one of the rear pair behind.
Both front players already provide depth. The left rear player can help the carrier by keeping a separate angle behind.
The fixo takes a small touch across the court, facing the right ala before the next pass.
The defender is on the inside shoulder. Turning into the middle brings the ball toward that pressure; the touchline side has room.
The defender has moved outside and can meet this carry. The fixo offers a pass away from that pressure.
After switching, the fixo moves behind the right ala to offer a return at a different angle.
This inside position stays near the defender’s screening line. Moving farther toward the touchline changes the angle from the fixo.
The defender has followed the left-side route. Passing there repeats the covered lane; the right ala gives a different angle.
After the lay-off, the pivot moves across to offer the fixo another forward lane.
The deeper pass is screened here. The defender followed the ball, leaving the outside runner available for the return.
The defender stayed with the outside route this time. The fixo is available behind the pivot, so keep the ball through that support.
The marker is on the pivot’s right shoulder. Turning right brings the next touch into the marker; the left side has room.
The marker has closed the turn. The right ala offers a lay-off that moves the ball around the pressure.
The left ala moves behind the receiver. The runner now has a return option after the diagonal pass.
The defender covers the right ala. The runner has gone down this same side, giving a different lane.

The left ala moves away from the end line to reconnect after the return pass.

A defender now covers the across-goal lane. The supporting pivot is behind the ball and offers a return route.
Blue carries wider. Our right ala follows under control, while the goalkeeper shifts with the shooting angle.
